title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
claim: In Ln3+ SMMs the spin–orbit coupling greatly exceeds the crystal-field splitting, so single-ion anisotropy of the crystal-field mJ states, rather than a strongly exchange-coupled multilevel spin, sets the anisotropy barrier.
explanation: The review contrasts this with transition-metal SMMs such as Mn12, where coupled spins give a large total S and a multilevel barrier. Internally shielded 4f orbitals make exchange very weak, so barrier height tracks the gap between opposite ±mJ directions and depends on the ion, site symmetry, and ligand electrostatics.
conditions: Strong spin–orbit coupling, stated as one to two orders of magnitude larger than the crystal-field splitting.
caveats: Polynuclear dipolar or exchange interactions can still modify relaxation even when single-ion anisotropy dominates.
